subject: LendWell compliance roundup + evidence delivery timeline
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>

Cc: Sophia Park <sophia.park@lendwell.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 7 Jun 2026 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: LendWell — compliance roundup + evidence delivery timeline

Hi Alex / Sophia,

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the straightforward discussion. Quick recap while it's fresh and a proposed evidence timeline so your procurement and security teams can plan.

High-level from our call (your priorities):
- Audit logs & retention: you need 7 years of retained audit logs for user-facing actions and the ability to export filtered event sets for audits.
- SOC 2 evidence: you require a redacted SOC 2 Type II (latest) and the control matrix mapping for data-in-transit / data-at-rest controls.
- Pen test summary: an executive summary and a redaction-friendly report for procurement review.
- DPA & retention terms: negotiate retention windows and delete-on-demand for sandbox/test data.

What we will provide (owner + ETA):
- Redacted SOC 2 Type II PDF + control narrative (Aditya) — by Tue 2026-06-09 EOD.
- 14-day audit log sample export (CSV/JSONL, redacted) + schema doc (Hannah) — by Mon 2026-06-08 noon PT.
- Pen-test executive summary + remediation tracker (security blurb only) — by Tue 2026-06-09.
- DPA draft excerpt showing retention clause options — Grace to share a proposed paragraph and open questions by Mon.

Immediate asks for you:
1) Confirm who on your side will be receiving evidence (email for portal delivery) — procurement@lendwell.com OK?
2) Any specific masking rules for PII in the audit sample? We will apply default redaction but can adapt.
3) Target date for procurement decision / PO? Helps us prioritize the depth of deliverables.

Attachments referenced: we will share the redacted SOC 2 and audit-log sample via Drive link (see below) — files are redacted for customer-specific data.

Next call suggestion: 30 minutes to walk your security lead through artifacts and mapping — Wed 2026-06-10 10:00–10:30 PT or Thu 06/11 09:00–09:30 PT.

I copied Aditya from our security team and Grace on commercial/contract items.

Thanks,
Hannah

Hannah Schmitt

Hannah — thanks, clear and helpful. Confirming a few items from our side after internal sync: 

- procurement@lendwell.com is the right delivery endpoint for the artifacts (please include our SOC/pen-test recipient: procurement@lendwell.com and our security owner sophia.park@lendwell.com).
- Masking rules: redact full account IDs and any payment instrument tokens; keep event timestamps and action types intact.
- For audit logs we mainly need auth events, admin role changes, API key rotation events, and data-export events over the 2-week sample.
- Timeline: procurement is aiming for a decision around Tue 2026-06-23; security wants to complete artifact review by 06/15 so they have a week buffer.

We'd like to see the control mapping (how your controls map to SOC criteria) with the SOC report. Also can you include a short note on how you isolate customer KV caches in shared pools? That's a technical question Sophia raised.

Either Wed 06/10 10:00 PT works for us for the walkthrough. I'll calendar-in once you confirm.

Best,
Alex

Looping in specifics from the security team — delivering the artifacts and answering Sophia's isolation question below.

Artifacts we will deliver (links + redaction notes):
- redacted_SOC2_report_2025-12.pdf (redacted Type II report, excludes customer identifiers and incident details).
- control_mapping_lendwell.csv (csv mapping SOC controls -> Redwood control owners) — included in Drive folder.
- audit_log_sample_2w_excerpt.jsonl (contains event_type, timestamp, resource_type, redacted_user_id) — PII redacted per request.
- pen_test_exec_summary_2025.pdf (one-page exec summary with severity breakdown).

Answers to Sophia's technical question (isolation of KV / cache):
- Logical isolation: customer sessions are namespaced; each customer's KV cache uses tenant-prefixed keys and per-tenant encryption keys.
- Process isolation: inference pools use multi-tenant runtime with process-level guardrails; critical secrets are never materialized in model KV caches.
- Fallback behavior: on eviction or failover, encrypted KV shards are moved with access controls; we provide audit entries for all eviction/restore events.

Delivery plan: I will upload redacted SOC and the audit sample to the Drive folder by Tue 2026-06-09 17:00 PT. Grace will share the DPA excerpt for negotiation on Mon 06/08.

Notes on pen-test: our last external pentest (2025-11) had two medium findings that were remediated and validated; we will not share full raw reports but will provide the executive summary and the remediation tracker. Procurement should escalate any follow-on asks to security@redwood.com.

Aditya Rao
